name: Chapter 4: Magical Factions

entries.title: Mages engage in a magical duel while members of the Crucible Keepers look on.

entries: Many scholars and practitioners of magic seek ever-greater prowess and status, but few can achieve these individually. Instead, those pursuing mystical knowledge often join influential groups. Numerous in membership and great in achievement, these factions accept adventurers into their folds, offering resources and knowledge in exchange for loyalty and service.

Each faction described in this chapter has its own outlook and goals, such as providing magical advice and entertainment to influence the powerful, researching alien forces from beyond the stars, and uncovering the secrets of life and undeath.

Faction members exchange magical discoveries, mentor pupils, and learn from more experienced colleagues. Members are united by shared specialties and philosophies. Although these organizations' disparate objectives often bring them into conflict with each other, members of different factions might also unite over common goals.
You can use these factions as patrons, as villains, or as organizations the characters can join. Adapt them to your world or campaign as needed.

entries.name: Faction Descriptions
entries: This chapter includes details on the following factions:

items: {@area Bejeweled Conclave.|1c8|x} The discreet enchanters of the Bejeweled Conclave make themselves invaluable to powerful clients as elite entertainers, advisers, and mediators while amassing clients' secrets.
{@area Bringers of Cosmic Dawn.|1d8|x} Reclusive transmuters obsessed with mutations, the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn seek guidance from alien intelligences.
{@area Covenant of the Grave.|1ed|x} The necromancers of the Covenant of the Grave study death and undeath with scientific precision, seeking esoteric knowledge through rigorous research.

{@area Crucible Keepers.|201|x} From volcanic eruptions to shore-shredding hurricanes, no natural disaster is too dangerous for the daring Crucible Keepers to study in their pursuit of ever-escalating applications for Evocation magic.
{@area Horizon Weavers.|213|x} The Horizon Weavers' conjurers practice summoning and teleportation as they explore and chart the multiverse.

{@area Ninth Quill.|224|x} The spies and saboteurs of the Ninth Quill steal lore and artifacts from other powerful mages; many members do so to safeguard these treasures, but others are motivated by greed. The Ninth Quill also stokes dissent among the other factions to keep them from growing too powerful.
{@area Phantasmic Circus.|239|x} The showy illusionists of the Phantasmic Circus entertain eager audiences with impossible spectacles.
{@area Seers of Sea and Sky.|24c|x} The diligent oracles of the Seers of Sea and Sky divine truths in the movements of the wind and waves.
{@area Sheltering Hands.|261|x} The abjurers of the Sheltering Hands uplift the downtrodden and protect those in need.

entries.name: Magical Specializations
entries: With the exception of the Ninth Quill, each of these magical factions specializes in a particular school of magic, as shown in the Factions by School table. Ninth Quill members instead dabble in all disciplines. These specializations are as much philosophical as technical. For instance, the fireball-throwing evokers of the Crucible Keepers are often forceful personalities who enjoy dramatic displays of destructive magic. In contrast, the subtle enchanters of the Bejeweled Conclave prefer to use smooth words to achieve their goals.

entries.name: Spellcasting Services
entries: Magical factions include spellcasters who specialize in the associated school of magic. A faction's base of operations counts as a city for the purpose of purchasing spellcasting services (described in the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB}) for spells of the associated school. At your discretion, the casting of spells that belong to other schools might also be available for purchase, and faction members might offer discounts based on the characters' relationship with the faction.

entries.name: Renown
entries: Characters can undertake missions and do favors for a faction and thereby earn renown with that faction without necessarily becoming members of the organization. Each faction description in this chapter includes benefits characters gain from accruing renown with the faction (as detailed in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG|2|Renown}).

entries.name: Joining Factions
entries: Although most members of magical factions are spellcasters, characters of any class can find a home in one or more of these factions. Each description includes the process for becoming a member of the faction; the benefits for doing so; and recommendations for classes, backgrounds, and proficiencies that make characters particularly well suited to the faction. The Factions by Class table provides a summary of which factions are a good fit for each class from the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB|3}.

entries.name: Special Facilities
entries: Each faction detailed in this chapter includes a special facility that members of that faction can add to their Bastions. The rules for Bastions appear in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG|10}.

entries.name: Faction Relationships
entries: The Faction Attitudes table summarizes the relationships between the factions described in this chapter. Faction pairs marked with an {@i F} consider each other allies; their members have a default attitude of {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} toward one another. Pairs marked with an {@i H} consider each other rivals; their members have a default attitude of {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} toward one another. Members of factions marked with an {@i I} begin as {@variantrule Indifferent [Attitude]|XPHB|Indifferent} toward one another. Exceptions might exist on an individual level.

entries.name: Bejeweled Conclave
entries: The Bejeweled Conclave is known as an organization of professional entertainers and mediators who cater to wealthy clients. They host glamorous parties, serve as courtiers, broker deals, and provide entertainment for exclusive functions.

But the Bejeweled Conclave wields far more influence than its publicly known services indicate. Consummate agents behind the throne, the enchanters of the Bejeweled Conclave cultivate elite connections and shift the balance of power in cities across the world.

entries.name: Goals and Activities

entries.title: This unassuming baker is, in reality, a member of the Bejeweled Conclave's Whisper Network.

entries: The Bejeweled Conclave seeks to increase its sway across the multiverse. The faction engages skilled diplomats, courtiers, and entertainers and hones their abilities. Enchanters and spies receive a more clandestine, but no less thorough, education. The conclave prizes subtlety and secrecy above all; members are taught that it's better to fail a mission and keep the conclave's secrets than to succeed at the cost of exposing the faction's true goals.

The Bejeweled Conclave operates in major cities throughout the multiverse. Distance keeps members from knowing all their peers, but the faction is quick to celebrate successes, building loyalty and camaraderie within its ranks. While all members learn conversational tricks to offer convincing praise, the compliments members bestow on each other are usually genuine.

Conclave members understand that overtly using Enchantment magic risks exposing them as more than entertainers and courtiers. If a member must modify a noble's memories or magically dominate a general, they undertake significant planning to conceal their involvement.

entries.name: Leadership and Organization
entries: More experienced members of the Bejeweled Conclave oversee operations assigned to junior members. Valuable secrets are reported through this hierarchy up to the faction's highest ranks, referred to as the Whisper Network. These leaders hoard a treasure trove of secrets; there are few facts about the movers and shakers of civilization that the Bejeweled Conclave doesn't know.

Conclave members are trusted to act alone when necessary, such as when an important client insists on hiring only a single mediator or companion. When possible, though, senior members politely request that their "junior clerks" or "associates in training" handle more workaday aspects of their affairs. Such requests, which might include subtle magical compulsion, are a ruse to bring another trained member to operate from the shadows. As a result, clients who planned to planned to hire only one member of the Bejeweled Conclave often find themselves engaging two or three.

entries.name: Whisper Network
entries: Members of the Whisper Network keep their identities private, even from their peers. The only exception is Madame Hestia Ilverne (Medium {@creature Noble Prodigy|XMM}), a courteous human Whisper Network member who heads the conclave's public-facing efforts. Rumors within the faction claim that Madame Ilverne is among the lowest ranked of the leaders, but she seems nothing but pleased with her position.

Whether members of the Whisper Network work as music instructors, clerks, dancers, or cooks, they keep an eye on all aspects of Bejeweled Conclave activities. If they have edicts or missions to impart, they do so through Madame Ilverne. When she casually mentions a task to a member with the words "The Network would prefer a favor," all comprehend the seriousness of the request.

entries.name: Lurewood Mansion
entries: A regal manor house in the garden district of a major city, Lurewood Mansion is the conclave's academy. The previous owners donated their property generations ago for unknown reasons. The manor's architecture has been adapted to include numerous salons and studies, as well as a fine kitchen.

In the studies, members of the Bejeweled Conclave learn to negotiate deals and defuse arguments. In the salons, singers, dancers, and musicians practice entertainment suitable for elevated private parties, from subdued chamber music to sensual dances to heart-wrenching ballads. New faction members take lessons here no matter how polished they are when recruited, if for no other reason than to bolster the illusion that negotiation and entertainment are the Bejeweled Conclave's prime objectives.

Beneath the mansion, a dizzying maze of chambers connected through locked doors and one-way mirrors facilitates practice in eavesdropping, lock-picking, quick changes, and stealthy escapes. Other rooms allow members to rest out of sight. The heart of the maze contains the mansion's best-kept secret: workrooms where enchanters teach apprentice mages the arts of twisting minds, magically hiding secrets, and erasing memories.

entries.name: Joining the Conclave
entries: Aspiring faction members can't join the Bejeweled Conclave by requesting admission; members inevitably deny that there are any openings in what they claim is simply a loose professional organization.

Entry is only by invitation. Senior members carefully watch entertainers and mediators who have impressive public reputations. Those who seem particularly shrewd and ambitious might receive an invitation for free training in their specialties at Lurewood Mansion, hosted by Madame Ilverne.

Once an invitee arrives, Madame Ilverne engages them in cryptic conversation. If the potential member impresses her with their poise, acumen, and discretion, she invites them to join the faction. Otherwise, she thanks them for their time and sends them on their way without ever indicating that the mansion is anything other than a professional academy.

entries.name: Renown Rewards
entries: Characters gain renown with the Bejeweled Conclave by sharing valuable secrets or completing conclave missions. As their Renown Scores increase, they gain access to various perks, as shown on the Bejeweled Conclave Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

entries.caption: Bejeweled Conclave Renown
rows: You can consult the Bejeweled Conclave before meeting a significant figure for the first time to learn a personal secret—humorous, embarrassing, or otherwise socially relevant—about that person.

You can stay in Lurewood Mansion or any other residence operated by the conclave, providing you a {@book Modest|XPHB|6|Modest (1 GP per Day)} lifestyle for free. If you have just returned from a dangerous locale, conclave members insist you first take a bath.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the Bejeweled Conclave gives you one Uncommon magic item—usually a Ring or a Wondrous Item.

Your lifestyle at Lurewood Mansion or any conclave residence increases to {@book Comfortable|XPHB|6|Comfortable (2 GP per Day)}. Additionally, you can request the aid of {@dice 1d4} {@creature Spy|XMM|Spies} for a mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
If you are arrested for anything short of treason in any land where the Bejeweled Conclave operates, the conclave finds a way to have your charges dismissed.
You can arrange for a meeting with Madame Hestia Ilverne. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the conclave teaches you its entrancing magic. You always have the {@spell Enthrall|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.

At your instruction, one of the conclave members casts {@spell Modify Memory|XPHB} (save {@dc 15}) for free on a target of your choice. You must have met or seen the target at least once within the last 30 days, and the spell is cast within 24 hours of you choosing your target. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

Members of the conclave openly share information with you. Additionally, the first time your Renown Score reaches 50, the Bejeweled Conclave imparts a significant secret about you that you didn't know. This secret is up to the DM and might take the form of a {@filter supernatural gift|rewards|type=blessing;charm} (see the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}).

entries.name: Bejeweled Conclave Characters
entries: Joining the Bejeweled Conclave is advantageous for any character with mysterious allure, regardless of whether they use magic to enchant others. Those skilled at uncovering and trading secrets are also well suited to this faction, as are entertainers who specialize in dancing, singing, or other performance arts.

The most sought-after recruits are {@class Bard|XPHB}, {@class Rogue|XPHB}, {@class Sorcerer|XPHB}, {@class Warlock|XPHB}, or {@class Wizard|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Wizard|XPHB|Enchanter|Enchanter|AU} subclass). Characters with proficiency in {@skill Deception|XPHB}, {@skill Performance|XPHB}, {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}, or {@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB} or who have the {@background Bejeweled Conclave Spy|AU}, {@background Entertainer|XPHB}, or {@background Noble|XPHB} background are also likely to be recruited.

entries.name: Member Benefits
entries: If you're a member of the Bejeweled Conclave, you receive these benefits.

entries.name: Finer Things
entries: The conclave ensures its members dress well, paying you a stipend that supports your {@book Wealthy|XPHB|6|Wealthy (4 GP per Day)} lifestyle (4 GP per day).

entries.name: Trinket
entries: Roll on the {@item Bejeweled Conclave Trinket|AU|Bejeweled Conclave Trinkets} table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the Bejeweled Conclave.

entries.name: Using This Faction
entries: As well-connected spies and secret keepers, members of the Bejeweled Conclave can provide characters with useful information. For example, the conclave might help the characters if they've lost a lead or are having trouble gaining access to an important public figure. The conclave might insist on a favor or secret in return, pulling the characters into its webs of intrigue.
The style of the Bejeweled Conclave involves elegance, manners, and class: all techniques to be admired. Just beware members' hidden agendas.

entries.name: Special Facility
entries: Members of the Bejeweled Conclave can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

entries.name: Bringers of Cosmic Dawn

entries.title: A member of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn transforms a colleague into a strange creature.

entries: A secretive organization of amoral transmuters, the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn receives abstruse directives from alien entities that hail from the dark spaces between stars. Faction members magically mutate plants and creatures in preparation for visitation by these beings—an event they believe is inevitable. They believe these entities will witness their glorious transmutations, be impressed, and bring about an exalted future full of mutated aberrations that serve transmuters' every whim.

entries.name: Goals and Activities
entries: The exact goals of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn are inscrutable to many members, though all believe they are helping to usher an ascended age of existence. The faction draws unprincipled transmuters, fringe scientists, and irrational astronomers to its academy and observatory, the Cosmic Oculus, where they receive fractured instructions from the faction's five leaders, known as the Starspeakers.

These communications have a consistent message: Faction members must transmute the flora and fauna surrounding the Cosmic Oculus. Invariably, this involves transforming plants into hostile, flesh-eating specimens and mutating beasts to rearrange organs, add joints to limbs, and cause them to secrete slime. In doing so, the faction hopes to gain the attention of alien entities they believe will descend and warp all worlds in their path.

The faction members are united in purpose but not in execution. Some pursue their own theories of mutation and transfiguration, experimenting on themselves as much as on other subjects. Some instructions communicated by the Starspeakers conflict with others, as though the alien entities they seek to communicate with weren't working in concert. These contradictions mean that the faction's work advances erratically, with rejected experiments as common as transformations deemed to be in concordance with the aliens' will.

entries.name: Dawnrise Canyon
entries: Bringers of Cosmic Dawn members carry out most transmutations far from public scrutiny. The faction is based in the secluded Dawnrise Canyon, far below the clifftop where the Cosmic Oculus stands. The once-tranquil canyon is now a dangerous valley of frightening creatures, hostile plants, aggressive transmuters, and wandering aberrations drawn to the unnatural landscape. Time moves erratically in the region thanks to frequent use of time-altering magic to speed up or slow down specific mutations.

entries.name: Opposition to the Far Realm
entries: While outsiders might not comprehend the distinction between the alien intelligences the Starspeakers commune with and the monsters of the Far Realm, Bringers of Cosmic Dawn members fear and reject the Far Realm as unknowable, indescribable, and inimical to life. The faction works to counter Far Realm incursions and expels any members who deal directly with that domain of incomprehensible horror.

entries.name: Leadership and Organization
entries: The Bringers of the Cosmic Dawn lacks a rigid hierarchy, but its leaders maintain careful control over the information they receive from both members' experiments and alien intelligences.

entries.name: Member Roles
entries: Certain members of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn have special roles in the faction.

entries.name: Starspeakers
entries: The five enigmatic Starspeakers command the entire faction. None answer to any name besides their title, and they rarely leave the Cosmic Oculus except to measure progress within Dawnrise Canyon. Four Starspeakers (Medium {@creature Aberrant Cultist|XMM|Aberrant Cultists}) are human. The fifth and most senior Starspeaker appears to be an elderly human astronomer, but she is actually a magically disguised {@creature Aboleth|XMM} who has eschewed the Far Realm.

entries.name: Worldwarpers
entries: Most faction members work at the Cosmic Oculus or Dawnrise Canyon, but others, called Worldwarpers, venture into civilized lands to engage in more far-flung experimentation. Worldwarpers seek out willing recipients to, as they put it, "gain blessings from beyond the stars."

Worldwarpers might offer to improve a banker's garden with voracious plants to deter thieves, provide an aberration to help guard a prison, or augment a diplomat's body to produce intoxicating pheromones. Like the work in Dawnrise Canyon, these puzzling changes ostensibly further a wider agenda, but Worldwarpers are rarely aware of the end goals; they merely put pieces in place as commanded and report back to the Starspeakers.

entries.name: Blots
entries: The Starspeakers secretly assign faction members to find and eradicate Far Realm sympathizers. These individuals, known within the faction as Blots, also venture into places where the Far Realm's stain bleeds into the world, seeking to quash the Far Realm's presence wherever they find it.

entries.name: Things Beyond the Stars
entries: The Bringers of Cosmic Dawn receives messages from many alien intelligences, not all of which are aligned with one another. You can use the Alien Entities table to generate sample intelligences that are directing the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn.
The multiverse is vast and full of entities you can't imagine. I judge not those who seek guidance from the stars—though if innocents come to harm, these experimenters will regret their choices.

entries.caption: Alien Entities
rows: Atropus, the World Born Dead, is a malevolent entity the size of a planetoid that drifts ever closer to the world.
Dendar, the Night Serpent, is a colossal beast that feeds on nightmares generated by its warped mind.
Tharizdun, the Chained God, is a dark spiral of roiling nothingness. It seeks freedom from its millennia-long imprisonment and the extinction of all life.
Xhalovix is an amalgamation of 9,999 mutated planets preparing to ascend to godhood once it has transformed its ten-thousandth world.

Trapped beneath a ruined city, Zargon the Returner seeks loyal worshippers to restore his mutation-steeped realm of slime and decadence. The dark sky reveals his malign will to those who know how to interpret it.
Ejected from the Negative Plane, a nameless evil entity drives mortals to despair by twisting reality into impossible forms.

entries.name: Joining the Bringers
entries: Transmuters might seek out the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn even if they don't wish to advance the faction's goals. Faction members are undeniable masters of Transmutation magic, and some daring characters might join long enough to learn their secrets. Although some transmuters escape the faction, far too many begin to believe the Starspeakers' ramblings and become devotees—or worse, they become unwilling subjects for experimental mutations when their disloyalty is uncovered.

entries.name: Cosmic Oculus
entries: Once an abandoned observatory, the Cosmic Oculus became the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn's base when the faction discovered that the facility seems to magically amplify the messages of entities between the stars. In addition to the Starspeakers, faction astronomers also live in the Cosmic Oculus to record psychic signals from deep space and make nightly measurements of celestial bodies.

Most faction members never see the inside of the Cosmic Oculus. The ramshackle buildings clustered along the cliff face between the observatory and the canyon have expanded and mutated on their own, and members have used spells such as {@spell Stone Shape|XPHB} and {@spell Fabricate|XPHB} to haphazardly extend walls, enclose laboratories, and create passageways through the rock.

entries.name: Renown Rewards
entries: Characters gain renown with the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn by engaging in aberrant transmutations or completing faction quests to recover rare ritual ingredients, samples of unusual flora and fauna, or astronomical measurements from distant locations. As their Renown Scores increase, characters gain access to various perks, as shown on the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

entries.caption: Bringers of Cosmic Dawn Renown
rows: You can freely enter Dawnrise Canyon, though you are afforded no specific protections from its dangers.
The Bringers of Cosmic Dawn warns you when you travel near places with Far Realm influence or a significant number of Aberrations.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn gives you an Uncommon magic item from the Scroll, Potion, or Wondrous Item category.

{@dice 1d4} {@creature Cultist|XMM|Cultists}, convinced you embody a prophecy, become your loyal followers. You can order this retinue to assist you for one mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
You can buy Common and Uncommon Spell Scrolls that contain Transmutation spells from faction members.
{@dice 1d4} {@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM|Cultist Fanatics} join your retinue of loyal followers.

The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the faction teaches you its transmuting magic. You always have the {@spell Alter Self|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
You can buy Rare Spell Scrolls that contain Transmutation spells from faction members.

Faction members openly share information with you. Additionally, the first time your Renown score reaches 50, you can undertake voluntary mutations to enhance your physiology. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws made to avoid or end the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} and {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} conditions.

entries.name: Bringers of Cosmic Dawn Characters
entries: Most members of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn are transmutation-focused mages, but any characters with an interest in astronomy, aberrations, or warping life are welcome. New recruits aren't permitted to balk at the faction's creations or goals.

The most welcome recruits are {@class Sorcerer|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Sorcerer|XPHB|Aberrant Sorcery|Aberrant|XPHB} subclass), {@class Warlock|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Warlock|XPHB|Great Old One Patron|Great Old One|XPHB} subclass), or {@class Wizard|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Wizard|XPHB|Transmuter|Transmuter|AU} subclass). Characters with proficiency in {@skill Arcana|XPHB}, {@skill Medicine|XPHB}, or {@skill Nature|XPHB} or with {@item Navigator's Tools|XPHB} are also valued as recruits, as are characters with the {@background Cosmic Dawn Experiment|AU}, {@background Guide|XPHB}, or {@background Hermit|XPHB} background.

entries.name: Member Benefits
entries: If you're a member of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn, you receive these benefits.

entries.name: Starwatcher Gear
entries: The Bringers of Cosmic Dawn provide you with {@item Navigator's Tools|XPHB} and a blank notebook in which to record your astronomical observations.

entries.name: Trinket
entries: Roll on the {@item Bringers of Cosmic Dawn Trinket|AU|Bringers of Cosmic Dawn Trinkets} table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn.

entries.name: Using This Faction
entries: The Bringers of Cosmic Dawn can easily serve as a villainous or amoral organization in your campaign. If the characters pursue villains to the Celestial Oculus, you can determine whether the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn fight the characters with the aid of powerful Transmutation magic and strange Aberrations, or if they turn out to be curious intellectuals duped by malign influences.

However, the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn need not be villains. The characters might need the faction's extensive knowledge of Transmutation magic to undo a shape-shifting curse or restore a transmuted ally to the proper form. Members' whispers about creatures from the depths of space might presage an incursion by conquering githyanki astride dragons or a fleet of mind flayers on spelljamming vessels.

entries.name: Special Facility
entries: Members of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

entries.name: Covenant of the Grave
entries: The Covenant of the Grave is a loose affiliation of necromancers and those interested in studying death and undeath through a disciplined, scientific lens. The covenant has no room for megalomaniacs who seek domination via hordes of undead minions.

These realists are aware that their studies, no matter how clinical, unnerve most people, so their members are unobtrusive and their laboratories hidden. The greatest covenant academy is the Pale Tower, a morbid, bone-white structure far from civilization.

entries.name: Goals and Activities
entries: Covenant members are typically more interested in deepening their knowledge than their power. They freely share their research with each other via correspondence, personal visits, or clandestine lectures, but they rarely reveal discoveries to those outside the organization. Many worry that their research might be misused for sinister, nonacademic ends. Others simply don't expect anyone but like-minded scholars to comprehend their work.

Unlike necromancers who incite undead uprisings, the Covenant of the Grave usually works to stymie undead hordes and return less powerful undead to the safer confines of the laboratory or grave. Members consider undead rampages dreadfully unscientific, if not outright embarrassing. They're keenly aware of the harm that such villainous necromancy brings to the faction's reputation. Their opposition to necromantic wickedness sometimes puts the faction in conflict with powerful undead such as liches, death knights, or vampires.

entries.name: Leadership and Organization
entries: Although an established hierarchy exists within the Covenant of the Grave, members are usually too engrossed in their own research to worry about rank.

entries.name: Necrodemics and Gravetenders
entries: Any faction member who shares a significant scholarly truth about death, decay, or undeath with the faction might gain the title of Necrodemic. Some members hold expanded titles such as Arisen Necrodemic or Necrodemic Embalmist, awarded for sharing more complex knowledge.

The title of Gravetender is held by the three head administrators of the Pale Tower. Emeritus administrators keep this title after retirement, so four to six Gravetenders usually exist at a time. Gravetenders set the overall direction for the faction but are usually bookish and circumspect, so change within the faction is gradual.

entries.name: Joining the Covenant

entries.title: Members of the Covenant of the Grave show respect to undead individuals who allow themselves to be studied.

entries: Any spellcaster with an interest in Necromancy magic or macabre research is likely to hear about the Covenant of the Grave, but the faction doesn't actively recruit. The covenant expects aspirants to independently identify its members and present a well-reasoned proposal for membership. A member who receives a qualified aspirant usually confers with other members before either taking on the aspirant as a research assistant or sending them to study at the Pale Tower.

entries.name: Undead Members
entries: Only a few members of the Covenant of the Grave are undead. Covenant members have little use for less powerful undead such as skeletons and zombies, and other undead are usually too consumed by their hungers to maintain the intellectual rigor the covenant expects. The Undead Members table details the few undead scholars in the covenant.

entries.caption: Undead Members
rows: A bookish {@creature Ghost|XMM} who haunts his surgical theater, Adlin is so tied to his experiments that he's unaware he's dead.
The Lawful Neutral {@creature Lich|XMM} Kadra hides that she's undead so her highly regarded insights into lichdom seem inspired by intellect rather than a study of her own nature.
A determined {@creature Revenant|XMM}, Melodin is a Gravetender of the Pale Tower who seeks to avenge herself against her predecessor by proving herself the superior administrator.

entries.name: The Pale Tower
entries: The greatest concentration of covenant members resides in the Pale Tower. Rising from a noxious swamp, this bone-white structure is thousands of years old. The tower's small, dingy exterior belies its underground warren of classrooms, laboratories, and ossuaries.

In addition to being an academy and research institution, the Pale Tower is a repository of sinister necromantic magic that the covenant doesn't want misused. Rumors hold that malicious artifacts, lost Necromancy spells, and soul-staining magic items are locked away in vaults only the Gravetenders can access.

entries.name: Renown Rewards
entries: Characters gain renown with the Covenant of the Grave by sharing scholarly insights into death or undeath or by completing quests for the Covenant. As their Renown Scores increase, characters gain access to various perks, as shown on the Covenant of the Grave Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

entries.caption: Covenant of the Grave Renown
rows: You receive free lodging at the Pale Tower and can access its extensive subterranean libraries. The covenant safely contains or destroys malevolent magic items you surrender to its care.
You can purchase the costly Material components required for Necromancy spells you can cast from covenant members.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the covenant gives you an Uncommon magic item from the Rod or Wand category.
Covenant members freely cast the {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell on you and your allies.

You earn the honorary title of Necrodemic. When you surrender a magic item to the covenant, the covenant gifts you a different magic item of an equal or lesser rarity from the same category as the surrendered item.
You can arrange for a meeting with any of the faction's Gravetenders. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the faction shares necromantic secrets with you. You always have the {@spell Speak with Dead|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.

You earn the honorary title of Arisen Necrodemic. You can request the help of {@dice 1d4} {@creature Mage|XMM|Mages} for one mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

If you or one of your allies dies and the body is brought to the Pale Tower, a covenant member casts a {@spell Resurrection|XPHB} spell, targeting the deceased. This reward is free the first time you use it. On subsequent occasions, you must provide any Material components normally consumed by the spell.

entries.name: Covenant of the Grave Characters
entries: Joining the Covenant of the Grave is advantageous to any character interested in the secrets of life and death. While intellectual rigor is important, knowledge of any death-adjacent subject is sufficient for aspiring members.

The most welcome aspirants are {@class Cleric|XPHB}, {@class Monk|XPHB}, and {@class Wizard|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Wizard|XPHB|Necromancer|Necromancer|AU} subclass). Characters with proficiency in {@skill Arcana|XPHB}, {@skill Investigation|XPHB}, or {@skill Medicine|XPHB}; proficiency with {@item Leatherworker's Tools|XPHB}; or the {@background Covenant of the Grave Recruit|AU}, {@background Sage|XPHB}, or {@background Scribe|XPHB} background are also good fits.

entries.name: Member Benefits
entries: If you're a member of the Covenant of the Grave, you receive these benefits.

entries.name: Grave Services
entries: The covenant respectfully performs final rites for your corpse whenever the inevitable comes to pass.

entries.name: Modest Lifestyle
entries: The covenant pays you a stipend that supports your {@book Modest|XPHB|6|Modest (1 GP per Day)} lifestyle (1 GP per day).

entries.name: Trinket
entries: Roll on the {@item Covenant of the Grave Trinket|AU|Covenant of the Grave Trinkets} table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the covenant.

entries.name: Using This Faction
entries: Faction members might warn the characters of potential necromantic uprisings or escort the party through lands plagued with undead. Having access to graveyards and burial houses, the faction might also recover the corpse of someone the characters want to revive or question.

The covenant isn't likely to aid the characters for free. Members might request lost necromantic lore in exchange for their help or task the party with defeating a necromancer or undead creature who has rejected the covenant's academic overtures.

entries.title: Two necromancers cast the {@spell Animate Dead|XPHB} spell on a nearby corpse in a graveyard.

entries.name: Special Facility
entries: Members of the Covenant of the Grave can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

entries.name: Crucible Keepers
entries: The Crucible Keepers consists of daredevil evokers who venture into natural or magical disasters to study the phenomenal power at play. Some members use their Evocation magic to counter disasters and help others, while other members revel in nature's destructive forces and take inspiration from them to enhance their own devastating spellcraft.

entries.name: Goals and Activities

entries.title: Crucible Keepers love a good explosion.

entries: Crucible Keepers study Evocation magic to command energy and control powerful forces. They eschew solitary scholarship, preferring informal gatherings where they exchange ideas and try to impress their peers with spectacular displays of magical might.

Faction members might be thrill seekers, but they aren't fools. They plan their dangerous endeavors well in advance, spending days or weeks charting natural or magical phenomena before enjoying the rush of soaring through the eye of a hurricane or surfing a lava flow. They employ protective magic while engaging in these endeavors, and they're quick to chide fools who confront danger unprepared.
Overuse of powerful evocation magic can warp the land as well as the souls of those who become drunk on magical power. The Crucible Keepers' attempt to right these wrongs is noble.

entries.name: Leadership and Organization
entries: Those drawn to the Crucible Keepers aren't the sort who like following orders. Ranks within the Crucible Keepers are unofficial, fluid, and based on frequent competitive challenges between members, with losers acknowledging winners' higher rank. Challenges usually involve magical duels, elaborate races, or dangerous stunts.

entries.name: Joining the Crucible Keepers
entries: The Crucible Keepers enthusiastically welcomes anyone who wants to try out for its ranks. Gaining membership is as simple as impressing any faction member with a clever display of Evocation magic, a wild physical stunt, or a dramatic parlor trick.

entries.name: Eljar Charscale
entries: The current head of the Crucible Keepers is a dragonborn named Eljar Charscale (Medium {@creature Evoker Archmage|AU}; see {@area chapter 6|30e|x}). Originally a human, Eljar was executed by cruel generals when he refused to use his magic in an unpopular war. After his allies reincarnated him, Eljar fled in his new dragonborn body. He took the name Charscale on joining the Crucible Keepers.

Eljar loves the thrill of Evocation magic and is undefeated in duels of spellcraft. In addition to his magical talent, Eljar is respected for listening to everyone and offering sensible guidance. He began leading the Crucible Keepers only a few months ago after the former leader died in a forest fire.

Eljar has a strong antiwar stance that he disseminates throughout the organization. He has forbidden members of the Crucible Keepers from serving as military battle mages. Some evokers believe this stance restricts their career paths, but most understand the reasoning behind Eljar's policy.

entries.name: Disaster Chasers
entries: Crucible Keepers predict and study natural and magical disasters, both to warn those who will be affected and to explore nature's incredible power. You can roll on or choose a result from the Pending Disasters table to generate a sample disaster Crucible Keepers plan to address.

entries.caption: Pending Disasters
rows: An undersea volcano near a busy bay is showing signs of an imminent eruption. Crucible Keepers who can operate underwater rush to study it and warn those nearby of its dangers.
Oracles predict a terrible earthquake will devastate a metropolis in the next few weeks. Crucible Keepers race to construct magical pylons to absorb its earth-rending energy.

A gate to the Elemental Plane of Fire is expected to appear in remote farmland. Crucible Keepers hope to stabilize and eventually close the gate—but before closing it, they want to venture through it to study planar conflagrations.

An ancient white dragon that planned to bury a peaceful valley beneath an avalanche has been slain. Crucible Keepers study the weakened snowpack so they can redirect the avalanche away from the nearby villages.

entries.name: Caldera Arcadium
entries: Although members believe that nature is the best classroom, the Crucible Keepers maintains a learning institution focused on Evocation magic. The Caldera Arcadium is a large stone building hanging over the rim of an active volcano, suspended by enormous metal chains and struts.

The temperature inside the building ranges from unpleasantly warm to blisteringly hot, but eager students fill its three classrooms every day. The building also holds magical forges for the study and creation of magic items. A stone bridge from the Arcadium's roof leads to dormitories, academic offices, and a cafeteria, all hanging off the volcano's edge.

The Caldera Arcadium's headmaster is a scholarly {@creature Efreeti|XMM} named Nadia Flameheart, who taught magic in the City of Brass for a millennium before joining the Crucible Keepers. The only wishes she entertains are those for better grades, and her only responses are tips for studying.

Fire-blackened {@creature Stone Golem|XMM|Stone Golems} called the Scorchborn provide security for the Arcadium, a duty that mostly involves defusing fights between hotheaded students. The Scorchborn are also instrumental to the wards that protect the school from volcanic eruptions, but not even Nadia Flameheart understands how. Since all Scorchborn are identical, no one is sure how many there are. No danger has yet presented a sufficient threat to marshal them all in one place.

Arcadium students frequently engage in death-defying stunts they call "field trips." The most common stunt is a leap from an Arcadium balcony during an eruption, trusting an ordinary rope to prevent a fall into lava. Another popular field trip involves launching homemade hang gliders from the volcano's edge.

entries.name: Renown Rewards
entries: Characters gain renown with the Crucible Keepers by surviving natural disasters or by completing Crucible Keeper missions. As their Renown Scores increase, characters gain access to various perks, as shown on the Crucible Keepers Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

entries.caption: Crucible Keepers Renown
rows: The Crucible Keepers sends you advance notice of natural disasters in your area.
The Crucible Keepers permits you and your companions to stay at the Caldera Arcadium.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the Crucible Keepers gives you an Uncommon magic item from the Wand or Weapon category.
You can buy Common and Uncommon Spell Scrolls that contain Evocation spells while at the Caldera Arcadium.

A reckless {@creature Mage Apprentice|XMM} becomes your loyal fan. You can order this apprentice to assist you for one mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
Eljar Charscale or Nadia Flameheart meets with you at your request. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the Crucible Keepers teaches you magic to guard you from the elements. You always have the {@spell Daylight|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
Faction members openly share information with you. You can buy Rare Spell Scrolls that contain Evocation spells while at the Caldera Arcadium.

You can call for an {@creature Efreeti|XMM} to aid you with a single task; the DM determines whether the efreeti can grant a {@spell Wish|XPHB}. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

entries.name: Crucible Keepers Characters
entries: The Crucible Keepers welcomes anyone willing to study destruction up close, which brings a high proportion of daredevils and thrill seekers into its ranks. Characters who are {@class Barbarian|XPHB}, {@class Druid|XPHB}, {@class Sorcerer|XPHB}, or {@class Wizard|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Wizard|XPHB|Evoker|Evoker|XPHB} subclass) are likely to be sought after as members, as are those with proficiency in {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}, {@skill Nature|XPHB}, or {@skill Survival|XPHB} or with the {@background Crucible Storm Chaser|AU} or {@background Noble|XPHB} background.

entries.name: Member Benefits
entries: If you're a member of the Crucible Keepers, you receive these benefits.

entries.name: Poor Lifestyle
entries: The Crucible Keepers pays you a stipend that supports a {@book Poor|XPHB|6|Poor (2 SP per Day)} lifestyle (2 SP per day).

entries.name: Trinket
entries: Roll on the {@item Crucible Keepers Trinket|AU|Crucible Keepers Trinkets} table to determine what trinket you have from your time in the Crucible Keepers.

entries.name: Using This Faction

entries.title: Members of the Crucible Keepers face each other in magical combat. It's harmless and all in good fun.

entries: Crucible Keepers are often harbingers of catastrophe. If they appear in large numbers, it's usually because they anticipate an imminent disaster. A Crucible Keeper traveling through a dangerous area might hire the party to escort them, but it would be wise to ask what awaits at the journey's end.

However, Crucible Keepers are evokers, not diviners, so their guesses are sometimes wrong. As the DM, you can decide whether that means the disaster doesn't happen, is earlier or later by days, or is some other event entirely.

Crucible Keepers also study the aftermath of disasters, both natural and magical. Their presence might be a detriment or a blessing for recovery efforts. Unscrupulous members revel in disasters' aftermath and might seek to profit from them, while selfless members work to ease suffering.

entries.name: Special Facility
entries: Members of the Crucible Keepers can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

entries.name: Horizon Weavers
entries: The Horizon Weavers is a collection of far-flung conjurers, explorers, and scholars who practice summoning, teleportation, and planar travel.

Members of the Horizon Weavers have unparalleled wanderlust; they've seen sights and lived through experiences most would consider too wild to be true. However, the faction's planar sojourns have not gone unnoticed, and members now work to avert the attention of a malevolent extraplanar entity fixated on their organization.

entries.name: Goals and Activities
entries: Horizon Weavers hone their expertise in all forms of Conjuration magic, from summoning to creation to teleportation, with a focus on extraplanar travel. Powerful Horizon Weavers create gates between planes, while junior members catalog known gates or simply wander through to see what's on the other side. New faction members usually begin by traveling their own world to experience different climates and cultures before exploring other planes.

Many faction members are also amateur or professional artisans; some weave textiles as well as magic. Horizon Weavers often incorporate spells such as {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} or {@spell Mage Hand|XPHB} into their everyday lives, using magic for everything from companionship to household chores.

entries.name: Horizon Weaver Cloaks
entries: Each new member who joins the faction receives a durable cloak with their initials sewn into the collar. Horizon Weavers recognize these garments on sight and seek to retrieve any that are lost or stolen.

A Horizon Weaver's cloak repels water and protects its wearer from most types of weather. The faction replaces damaged cloaks when necessary. Some members weave the threads of former cloaks into new ones.

Many Horizon Weavers incorporate their cloaks into magic items they create. The most popular choices are {@item Cape of the Mountebank|XDMG}, {@item Cloak of Protection|XDMG}, and {@item Clothes of Mending|XDMG}.

entries.name: The Lurker
entries: A massive beast from the liminal space between planes menaces the Horizon Weavers. This entity, known as the Lurker, towers higher than mountains, with immense pincers and a single, enormous eye that radiates malice and reflects strange lights and lines.

Several months ago, when faction members first glimpsed the Lurker, a powerful team of Horizon Weavers set out to confront the monster. The team went missing, and the Lurker has since become more aggressive, snapping at some Horizon Weavers in the split second it takes them to magically travel between planes. Sometimes this shears the unlucky traveler in half; other times, the individual never reappears. These incidents are rare, but all Horizon Weavers worry about a potential Lurker strike with each planar trip.
Those who provide shelter and aid to explorers of this vast multiverse are friends to both me and Mystra.

entries.name: Leadership and Organization
entries: As befits members of a society of explorers, Horizon Weavers are widely scattered. A wandering Horizon Weaver might go weeks or months without seeing another member, and a meeting might be coincidental. Senior faction members, called Gatemakers, settle disputes or provide advice, although reaching a Gatemaker often requires a cross-planar trek.

entries.title: When necessary, members of the Horizon Weavers call on powerful allies from other planes of existence.

entries.name: Way Stations and Shuttles
entries: Not all Horizon Weavers seek endless travel. Some stay in one place for months or years, perhaps with a friend or lover they met during their travels. Horizon Weavers who remain in one place are expected to maintain way stations, providing directions, supplies, and shelter to passing faction members.

Weaving slang is common in these way stations: a "shuttle" is a traveler, a "beam" is a well-established way station, a "weft" is a member with irrepressible wanderlust, and a "heddle" is someone reliable.
You can roll on the Planar Way Stations table to generate a sample way station or odd planar locale.

entries.caption: Planar Way Stations
rows: A gnome named Molly Nettle (Small {@creature Conjurer Archmage|AU}) keeps a gingerbread house in the {@book Feywild|XDMG|5|Feywild} where she welcomes Horizon Weavers but shoos away all others. She doesn't understand why visitors find her residence and her child-shaped cookie sculptures off-putting.

The Tidepool Larder is an air-filled grotto on the Elemental Plane of Water, stocked with salted fish and other seafood. The reclusive {@creature Marid|XMM} caretaker, Baliob, hides from visitors and doesn't charge for supplies.
A dour {@creature Githzerai Psion|XMM} named Ut maintains a peaceful monastery called Ninebells on a rocky island in Limbo. Ut lets non-Horizon Weavers stay no more than nine hours.

Scuttlebeam is a beached ship in a Feywild forest. Its married keepers, a goliath named Rusty Jenk (Medium {@creature Pirate Captain|XMM}) and an orc named Trellie (Medium {@creature Mage|XMM}), don't remember how the ship got here.
Falling Up, a floating inn in the Elemental Plane of Air, is managed by three human, semiretired Horizon Weavers (Medium {@creature Mage|XMM|Mages}), all eager to swap tales.
A way station in Bytopia called the Shuttle's Rest was recently reduced to ruins by an enormous, clawed creature.

entries.name: Joining the Horizon Weavers
entries: Any curious adventurer who longs to explore the unknown might join the faction after meeting a Horizon Weaver. An extended conversation with a member is all it takes to earn a second meeting, when the member presents the aspirant with a Horizon Weaver cloak and officially inducts them into the organization. An inducting member without weaving skills or connections might invite the new member to create their own Horizon Weaver cloak, though it must be made to the faction's specifications.

entries.name: Spiral Conservatory
entries: Deep in a forest on the Material Plane stands a twisting building of wood and stone that surrounds a grassy courtyard. This is the Spiral Conservatory, the first and largest Horizon Weaver way station. Here, students of Conjuration magic and planar lore learn to navigate hazardous environments, summon helpful creatures, and conjure useful equipment.

The Spiral Conservatory is located at a confluence of ley lines that provides numerous, if inconstant, gates to Arcadia, the Beastlands, and the Feywild. Fey and intelligent animals often wander through the Spiral Conservatory; some of them delight in mentoring eager Horizon Weavers.

A tiefling named Gallinaver the Heddle (Medium {@creature Conjurer Archmage|AU}; {@area chapter 6|30f|x}) serves as the Spiral Conservatory's chief caretaker. Gallinaver and his husband, a soft-spoken {@creature Djinni|XMM} named Cloud Lace, are the easiest Gatemakers to contact, as they're never far from the Spiral Conservatory.

entries.name: Renown Rewards
entries: Characters gain renown with the Horizon Weavers by displaying planar knowledge, conjuring magical wonders, reporting previously unknown planar gates, or completing excursions for the faction. As their Renown Scores increase, characters gain access to various perks, as shown on the Horizon Weavers Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

entries.caption: Horizon Weavers Renown
rows: You can consult with the Horizon Weavers to receive general information about a plane you intend to visit.
You can stay in any way station maintained by a Horizon Weaver (including the Spiral Conservatory).

The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the faction gives you an Uncommon magic item from the Armor or Wondrous Item category. Alternatively, if you're a member, the faction can craft your faction cloak into an Uncommon magic item of your choice.
You receive a 10 percent discount when buying armor, weapons, and adventuring gear from a Horizon Weaver way station.

You are given one of a pair of {@item Sending Stones|XDMG}; the other is held by a mid-level faction member. If you are lost in an extraplanar location the faction can reach, you can use the Sending Stone to call the faction for help. {@dice 1d4} {@creature Scout Captain|XMM|Scout Captains} then arrive to escort you to a safe destination. If your Renown Score drops below 20, your Sending Stone is confiscated.
The discount you receive at way stations increases to 20 percent.

The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the faction teaches you to traverse liminal spaces. You always have the {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
You can arrange for a meeting with any of the faction's Gatemakers. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

Faction members can cast the {@spell Plane Shift|XPHB} spell at your behest, transporting you and your allies to an extraplanar location of your choice. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

entries.name: Horizon Weavers Characters
entries: The Horizon Weavers welcome carefree, capable wanderers who yearn to see what's over the horizon or through a planar portal.

{@class Druid|XPHB}, {@class Ranger|XPHB}, and {@class Wizard|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Wizard|XPHB|Conjurer|Conjurer|AU} subclass) are excellent fits. Characters with proficiency in {@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB}; proficiency with {@item Navigator's Tools|XPHB} or {@item Weaver's Tools|XPHB}; or the {@background Artisan|XPHB}, {@background Guide|XPHB}, {@background Horizon Weaver Initiate|AU}, or {@background Wayfarer|XPHB} background are also welcome.

entries.name: Member Benefits
entries: If you're a member of the Horizon Weavers, you receive these benefits.

entries.name: Traveling Cloak
entries: You receive a distinctive Horizon Weavers cloak and a set of {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}.

entries.name: Trinket
entries: Roll on the {@item Horizon Weavers Trinket|AU|Horizon Weavers Trinkets} table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the Horizon Weavers.

entries.name: Using This Faction
entries: The Horizon Weavers might give out quests, such as mapmaking or rescue missions, that require travel to distant places. They might also seek the adventurers' help dealing with the threat of the {@area Lurker|216|x}.

The Horizon Weavers can also rescue characters stranded in distant or inhospitable places, such as those sent to other planes by the {@spell Prismatic Spray|XPHB} or {@spell Prismatic Wall|XPHB} spell. Lost characters might be lucky enough to find a Horizon Weaver way station.

entries.name: Special Facility
entries: Members of the Horizon Weavers can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

entries.name: Ninth Quill

entries.title: Members of the Ninth Quill plot the heist of magical lore.

entries: The Ninth Quill is a faction of thieves, saboteurs, and spies who use magic to obtain and sequester powerful artifacts and knowledge by any means necessary—including robbing and sabotaging other factions. The faction's leaders consider their organization to be superior to factions focused on a specific school of magic and the safest custodian of dangerous lore and relics, but some members also steal valuables and undermine other organizations for personal gain.

entries.name: Goals and Activities
entries: Ninth Quill members' adaptability and diverse areas of expertise help them infiltrate other groups, often posing as new recruits or long-absent members from other lands.
The Ninth Quill has a few popular catchphrases that members use as meaningful mantras—or excuses for criminality. These phrases are described in the sections that follow.

entries.name: Our Hands Are Safest
entries: Ninth Quill members often steal magic items and research to keep them out of others' hands. They receive extensive training in handling dangerous artifacts and resisting the influence of sentient objects. In principle, these items are sequestered in the Ninth Quill vaults (which members insist are more secure than any other faction's), but less scrupulous members might keep certain items for their own use.

entries.name: Others Learn So We Can Earn
entries: When the Ninth Quill steals discoveries and relics that aren't particularly harmful, it sells them to wealthy patrons to fund its operations. Desperate buyers rebuffed by other factions, such as a necromancer rejected by the {@area Covenant of the Grave|1ed|x} or a transmuter suspicious of the {@area Bringers of Cosmic Dawn|1d8|x}, might seek the services of the Ninth Quill to obtain such objects.

entries.name: Discontent Is Our Best Defense
entries: The Ninth Quill seeks to destabilize other factions that become too powerful. This often involves agents infiltrating a faction, then undertaking whisper campaigns, sabotaging experiments, and encouraging critical personnel to depart. The Ninth Quill agents quietly slip away once they have stoked sufficient inefficiency, paranoia, and infighting.

entries.name: Leadership and Organization
entries: The Ninth Quill values intelligence, resourcefulness, and loyalty. A significant majority of Ninth Quill agents use spellcasting to enhance their spy craft.

entries.name: A Careful Hierarchy
entries: Although Ninth Quill leaders take pains to hide their identities, the faction operates under a strict hierarchal system. Agents are the lowest ranking, followed by Lieutenants, followed by Masters. Those in the highest echelon are Guild Masters.

entries.name: Joining the Ninth Quill
entries: The Ninth Quill operates in the shadows and therefore doesn't entertain applicants. However, the Guild Masters keep an eye on talented thieves and other morally ambiguous individuals with magical skills. If the Guild Masters believe such an individual would be an asset to the Ninth Quill, they extend an invitation to visit Blackscript College—through an anonymous courier, of course.

entries.name: Blackscript College
entries: The hidden academy where the Ninth Quill trains its members is located in a crime-ridden neighborhood of a busy trade city. Dilapidated warehouses, all owned by the Ninth Quill, surround the college to ensure its privacy. There's no readily apparent entrance; instead, it's accessible only by unmarked doors in twisting alleys and hidden passages.

The centuries-old college was once a legitimate magical academy, but city records show that it closed decades ago due to administrative corruption. In truth, the college simply went underground to teach magical spy craft and thievery.

A former instructor at Blackscript College's predecessor academy, the college's dean is the elf Sirethe Slipshadow (Medium {@creature Spy Master|XMM}). Slipshadow is infamous for her ability to impersonate others and uses these skills to observe students during their studies and on early missions.

The college's library, called the Repository, holds an eclectic variety of stolen treasures. An adjacent chamber called the Ersatz Repository contains worktables where members make high-quality counterfeits of spellbooks, relics, and artifacts. Many cherished treasures held by other factions are actually Ninth Quill counterfeits.

entries.name: Renown Rewards
entries: Characters gain renown with the Ninth Quill by completing Ninth Quill missions or by contributing stolen magical lore or magic items. As their Renown Scores increase, characters gain access to various perks, as shown on the Ninth Quill Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

entries.caption: Ninth Quill Renown
rows: You and your companions receive free lodging at Ninth Quill safe houses, which are present in many cities.
You can buy Common potions and Spell Scrolls from Ninth Quill members.

If the authorities are searching for you, the Ninth Quill dispatches numerous faction members who are magically disguised to look like you. This might allow you to evade capture for days or months, at the DM's discretion. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 15, the Ninth Quill gives you an Uncommon magic item from the Repository.
You receive a magical decoder that allows you to read written Thieves' Cant. If your Renown Score drops below 20, this decoder is confiscated.

The Ninth Quill can provide you with a believable but useless duplicate of a magic item you show them. Creating the duplicate takes {@dice 1d4} days of work. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, Ninth Quill faction members teach you how to magically shroud yourself. You always have the {@spell Nondetection|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
You can buy Uncommon and Rare potions and Spell Scrolls from Ninth Quill members.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 50, the Ninth Quill gives you a Very Rare magic item that another faction desperately wants to recover.

entries.name: Ninth Quill Characters
entries: The Ninth Quill uses thieves and enforcers, but the group is no mere criminal guild; its leaders prefer recruits who have magical skill or knowledge.

The most welcome are {@class Bard|XPHB}, {@class Fighter|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Fighter|XPHB|Eldritch Knight|Eldritch Knight|XPHB} subclass), {@class Rogue|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Rogue|XPHB|Arcane Trickster|Arcane Trickster|XPHB} subclass), {@class Warlock|XPHB}, or {@class Wizard|XPHB}. Characters with proficiency in {@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill Deception|XPHB}; the {@background Agent of the Ninth Quill|AU}, {@background Charlatan|XPHB}, or {@background Criminal|XPHB} background; or the {@feat Magic Initiate|XPHB} feat are also valued.

entries.name: Member Benefits
entries: If you're a member of the Ninth Quill, you receive these benefits.

entries.name: Modest Lifestyle
entries: The Ninth Quill pays you a stipend to support your {@book Modest|XPHB|6|Modest (1 GP per Day)} lifestyle (1 GP per day).

entries.name: Trinket
entries: Roll on the {@item Ninth Quill Trinket|AU|Ninth Quill Trinkets} table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the Ninth Quill.

entries.name: Using This Faction
entries: The Ninth Quill often opposes other magical factions. You might introduce Ninth Quill {@creature Bandit|XMM|Bandits} or {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts} looking to steal the characters' hard-won items or lore, or you could establish intrigue-laden plots about Ninth Quill {@creature Spy|XMM|Spies}, {@creature Spy Master|XMM|Spy Masters}, or {@creature Bandit Deceiver|XMM|Bandit Deceivers} who stoke rivalries and paranoia within another faction.

Alternatively, the Ninth Quill could employ or aid the characters. The faction might recruit the characters to retrieve a valuable asset or assist them with recovering and disposing of a dangerous artifact. You could even build a campaign around efforts to steal relics from each of the other magical factions.
Good intentions are commonplace among members of the Ninth Quill, but never drop your guard around them.

entries.name: Special Facility
entries: Members of the Ninth Quill can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

entries.name: Phantasmic Circus

entries.title: Members of the Phantasmic Circus prepare for a magic-enhanced performance.

entries: Part entertainers' alliance and part traveling carnival, the Phantasmic Circus is an organization of performers and illusionists who create grand spectacles and share magical techniques to delight, entertain, and misdirect.

entries.name: Goals and Activities
entries: The Phantasmic Circus stages elaborate performances across the world, moving from city to city to bring delight and wonder. These performances are huge extravaganzas involving dozens of entertainers and drawing large audiences. The circus is renowned for illusions and pyrotechnics that reach hundreds of feet into the air.

These complex routines change with every show; Phantasmic Circus performers are always experimenting with new illusions, death-defying stunts, and musical accompaniment. Tickets and concessions are pricey, but audience members remember the faction's thrilling spectacles for the rest of their lives.

The Phantasmic Circus's performances use trained creatures for certain acts, but audience members would be shocked to realize how few genuine creatures are on display. Lifelike illusions of animals and monsters perform most stunts, while living animals are treated carefully and kept out of danger.

entries.name: One Circus, Many Troupes
entries: The Phantasmic Circus isn't a single traveling troupe, but rather the collective name for several groups that operate independently, each under the guidance of a manager called a Wondermaker. Circus members might shift from group to group to hone their skills, so residents of a city might never realize that the "Phantasmic Circus" that visited twice the previous year was actually two different troupes.

entries.name: Leadership and Organization
entries: The astounding and popular Phantasmic Circus of today had humble beginnings as a small traveling carnival called the Hayver and Hayver Circus. When the Hayvers' youngest sibling, the human Della, returned to the family circus with training in Illusion magic and a gregarious gnome husband named Walnip Waddlebell, the circus started its meteoric rise.

Soon, Della and Walnip were running the circus as its ringmasters and self-appointed "First Maestros." The couple also gave the increasingly illusion-focused show a flashier name. The other Hayvers have since passed away, but the aging First Maestros (both Small {@creature Performer Legend|XMM|Performer Legends}), still plan spectacles, train new illusionists, and orchestrate the many troupes operating as the Phantasmic Circus.

entries.name: Wondermakers
entries: The First Maestros are now too old to tour, but they keep in touch with each troupe as its travels bring it back to the circus's headquarters, the Mirage Lyceum. The First Maestros appoint a Wondermaker to guide each troupe. Most Wondermakers are flashy showoffs or grand illusionists who enjoy the spotlight as ringmasters or star performers. In other troupes, the Wondermaker works behind the scenes, guiding the performers and pushing their shows to new heights.

Each Wondermaker keeps their troupe's books, protects its members, makes its travel plans, and coordinates with other Wondermakers to ensure they aren't revisiting cities too soon. They also send performers from troupe to troupe to teach gifted members additional skills or to resolve personality clashes.

entries.name: Roustabouts
entries: Although acrobats, illusionists, animals, and entertainers are the stars of the Phantasmic Circus, a platoon of supporters keeps the troupe running. Collectively called roustabouts, these laborers and guides let the performers take the glory while collecting reasonable pay from the troupe's Wondermaker. The visual artists who design the elaborate sets and costumes are also roustabouts; they mentor each other to hone their artistic skills.
Mystra smiles on those who pluck the Weave to provide entertainment to the public. So do I—as long as that entertainment cloaks no foul deeds.

entries.name: Circus Acts
entries: No two Phantasmic Circus performances are the same. Roll on the Phantasmic Circus Acts table to generate a sample act as a basis for other wondrous spectacles.

entries.caption: Phantasmic Circus Acts
rows: Several Gladiators fight a beholder, which is an illusion—a hidden {@creature Performer Legend|XMM} uses the {@spell Major Image|XPHB} spell to simulate the monster.
Six trained mammoths form a pyramid, and a giant toad hops up to the top; all the animals are realistic illusions.
A {@creature Performer Maestro|XMM} sings an eerie ballad about a shipwreck while {@creature Performer|XMM|Performers} on trapezes swing over and through the illusion of a grand, doomed galley.
Two {@creature Satyr|XMM|Satyrs} play a compelling melody while they lead volunteers from the audience through a cage of glaring lions; the volunteers and lions are illusions.
Two {@creature Knight|XMM|Knights} joust while riding horses cloaked in illusions to look like rhinoceroses.
A {@creature Performer Maestro|XMM} navigates a wondrous illusory forest and grows 50 feet tall to step over the tallest tree at the act's conclusion.

entries.name: Joining the Phantasmic Circus
entries: Joining the Phantasmic Circus as a performer requires rigorous tryouts under the watchful eye of a troupe's Wondermaker, who makes final decisions about applicants. Those who wish to join the circus as roustabouts, however, need only express interest and demonstrate a relevant skill to a Wondermaker, who is usually happy to accept the additional help.

entries.name: Mirage Lyceum
entries: The headquarters of the Phantasmic Circus, the Mirage Lyceum, was formerly the winter home of the Hayver and Hayver Circus. Once a sad collection of animal pens and bunk rooms, it is now a vibrant jumble of playhouses, amphitheaters, classrooms, and studios.

The Mirage Lyceum puts on informal performances year-round. Some performers simply want to show their skills to the First Maestros; others are junior members who aren't yet ready to take to the road. This mingling of eager pupils and wise mentors makes the Mirage Lyceum an excellent place for any illusionist to learn.

Audiences come from miles around to view these informal performances, which are cheaper than the big-city spectacles. Some wonder-struck visitors stay for long periods, and a few become inspired to join the circus life.

entries.name: Renown Rewards
entries: Characters gain renown with the Phantasmic Circus by contributing illusory spectacles or by completing missions for the circus. As their Renown Scores increase, they gain access to various perks, as shown on the Phantasmic Circus Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

entries.caption: Phantasmic Circus Renown
rows: You can travel with the Phantasmic Circus, receiving food and cramped lodging (a {@book Poor|XPHB|6|Poor (2 SP per Day)} lifestyle) while you do. You can attend performances for free.
After a performance, faction members freely share with you {@dice 1d6} rumors heard from the audience members.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the Phantasmic Circus gives you an Uncommon magic item from the Wand or Wondrous Item category.

A troupe of {@dice 1d3 + 1} {@creature Performer|XMM|Performers} become your loyal followers. The troupe performs simple tasks, such as restocking supplies or gathering information, but they won't willingly put themselves in danger.
You can buy Common and Uncommon Spell Scrolls that contain Illusion spells from faction members.

Your troupe gains an additional {@dice 1d4} {@creature Performer|XMM|Performers}. Additionally, you can ask your troupe to help you with one dangerous mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, circus members share their illusory tricks with you. You always have the {@spell Mirror Image|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.

You can arrange for a meeting with any of the faction's Wondermakers or, when at the Mirage Lyceum, with the First Maestros. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
{@dice 1d4} {@creature Performer Maestro|XMM|Performer Maestros} and an additional {@dice 1d6} {@creature Performer|XMM|Performers} join your troupe.

entries.name: Phantasmic Circus Characters
entries: The Phantasmic Circus welcomes artists, entertainers, and illusionists of all types as performers, provided they impress a Wondermaker. Roustabouts can be of any class or background.

{@class Bard|XPHB}, {@class Rogue|XPHB}, and {@class Wizard|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Wizard|XPHB|Illusionist|Illusionist|XPHB} subclass) are excellent fits, as are characters with proficiency in {@skill Performance|XPHB} or with the {@background Charlatan|XPHB}, {@background Entertainer|XPHB}, {@background Phantasmic Circus Trouper|AU}, or {@background Wayfarer|XPHB} background.

entries.name: Member Benefits
entries: If you're a member of the Phantasmic Circus, you receive these benefits.

entries.name: Patron Connections
entries: You can always find work as an entertainer while in a settlement.

entries.name: Poor Lifestyle
entries: The circus provides you with performance proceeds to support your Poor lifestyle (2 SP per day).

entries.name: Trinket
entries: Roll on the {@item Phantasmic Circus Trinket|AU|Phantasmic Circus Trinkets} table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the Phantasmic Circus.

entries.name: Using This Faction
entries: You can use the Phantasmic Circus in your campaign to enliven an urban atmosphere. Since the Phantasmic Circus travels from city to city, the characters also might encounter the faction on the road.

The Phantasmic Circus cares more about presenting grand spectacles than following local laws. As such, the circus might create inadvertent fires or spark a panicked stampede that requires the characters' intervention. Alternatively, the circus might agree to conceal fugitives who don't seem harmful, possibly enabling the party to escape a settlement without alerting the authorities.

entries.name: Special Facility
entries: Members of the Phantasmic Circus can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

entries.name: Seers of Sea and Sky
entries: The Seers of Sea and Sky is a faction of oracles who make predictions about the future based on movements of the clouds and waves. Open to all methods of divination, the seers encourage communication with a wide array of aerial and undersea prophets and meticulously record their prognostications.

entries.name: Goals and Activities
entries: The Seers of Sea and Sky maintains libraries and reading rooms in many large, coastal cities. Within these hubs, seers cast Divination spells for reasonable costs; train other members in divination techniques; and maintain contact with visionaries across, above, and below the seas.
